name: M. Quinn, brewery

proprietors.name: Martin Quinn
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Martin Quinn is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at brewer in the north division (slot trade_households:persons/male/30_39/north/family/trade:brewer:002), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. One quota, filled once: this house is the establishment that head keeps.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a brewery kept by a north-division household deals this house onto North Water Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the December 1835 State census counts more of its class than the register holds. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The census that orders it was taken in December 1835 and counts a standing trade, not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read irish: Martin Quinn (irish). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real house of this class in the north division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn.

basis.note: the December 1835 State census prints 2; the register holds 1 at the scene date. The book leaves 1 of this class to reconstruct and this is one of them. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: the initial-and-surname signature is the commonest in the corpus — 'B. Jones, grocery and provision store', 'S. B. Cobb, saddle, harness and trunk manufactory'. The goods line is the only word the corpus prints for this class: the register carries one brewery, 'the Chicago Brewery', with no goods line under it, so the trade word stands alone rather than a list being composed for it. A TIGHTER COUNT STANDS UNAPPLIED, AND THIS RECORD CARRIES IT. The book takes its target from the December 1835 State census, which prints two breweries. But the Chicago American of 15 August 1835 takes stock of the town six weeks AFTER the scene date and counts 'one brewery, one furnace (just going up)' — one, where December counts two. If the American is right for 1 July 1835 then the town's second brewery arrived in the autumn and this house does not stand at the scene date at all. That is the Sept-Dec 1835 crosswalk's ruling to make and it has not made it: this bucket reads `compared_by_the_crosswalk: true` and `crosswalk_note: null`. The house therefore stands on the book's quota, with the count that would retire it printed here; a crosswalk that rules the American in re-cuts the bucket and --build withdraws this record, which is the only way it may ever go.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: a source naming a real house of this class, or a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders this bucket; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
